annotations.title: Claim a statement dropped on the website

description:
Claim every bank statement the user dropped on Well's website in one visit, using the ONE claim token from their message or from the /import-statement command argument, or the one claim link from Well's website that carries it (https://wellapp.ai/find-missing-invoices/#claim=...). Pass the link exactly as given; the tool reads the token out of it.

The token covers every file in that drop: call this tool once per token, never per file. It works once and expires an hour after the drop.

Returns one document_id per file; poll well_get_statement_import_result for each.

A refused token (expired, already claimed, unknown) is final: tell the user plainly and ask them to attach the files here, never retry. Files listed under failed were claimed but did not ingest; ask for exactly those by hand.

claim_token.description: The drop's claim token, or the claim link from Well's website that carries it, exactly as written: from the argument after /import-statement or from the user's message. Single-use, covers every statement in that drop, expires one hour after the drop.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A retried write with the same key returns the original result instead of re-applying the operation.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several — a write lands in exactly one workspace and this call would not say which.

name: well_claim_statement_draft

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

documents.description: One entry per file that reached the import pipeline.

deduplicated.description: True when an identical document was already in the workspace, so nothing was imported twice.

document_id.description: Poll well_get_statement_import_result with this id for the import outcome.

ordinal.description: The file's 0-based index among the files Well accepted from the drop, in arrival order.

drop_id.description: The drop this token belonged to. Safe to quote; the token is not.

failed.description: Files that were claimed but did not ingest. Their bytes are gone; ask the user for exactly these by name.

newly_connected.description: Tools that connected to this workspace since the last result and that no session was told about yet, oldest first. Present only when at least one tool is new. Start the reply with one line per entry, in the person's language: "<name> is connected.". Never fold several entries into one sentence. Each entry comes back once, on one result only: never repeat its line later.
